claim_tested: AS-B has two active sites joined by an intramolecular ammonia tunnel; Cys1 is the glutaminase nucleophile
key_finding: Glutamine-site residues Arg49, Asn74, Glu76, Asp98 position the glutamine substrate; Cys1 is the N-terminal nucleophile; the two sites are ~20 A apart and connected by a tunnel
context: E. coli asparagine synthetase B, C1A mutant co-crystallised with Gln and AMP
confidence_and_limitations: High for the reference site definition. A bacterial enzyme is used as the template for a human protein; the tunnel in the crystal is partly substrate-induced.

evidence_type: primary, enzyme kinetics, isotope transfer, positional isotope exchange
claim_tested: A carboxylate at the AS-B Glu348 position is required for beta-aspartyl-AMP formation
key_finding: Mutation of Glu348 abolishes asparagine production; the paper states that formation of the intermediate and therefore asparagine production depends on a carboxylate side chain at this position
context: E. coli AS-B, purified recombinant enzyme
confidence_and_limitations: High. This is a direct functional test of the exact residue ASNSD1 lacks. Transfer to human ASNSD1 is by structural equivalence, not by assay.

claim_tested: The Glu348/349 carboxylate is curated as important for beta-aspartyl-AMP intermediate formation
key_finding: UniProt carries a SITE feature at this residue derived from PMID:20853825
confidence_and_limitations: Database-level support only; traced back to the primary paper above.

citation: This run: structural superposition of AF-Q9NWL6-F1 onto 1CT9 chain A (provenance/structural_mapping.json)
claim_tested: Does ASNSD1 retain both domains and an N-terminal Cys?
key_finding: Both domains superpose on AS-B: GATase 1.74 A over 110 CA, synthetase 1.38-1.56 A over 90-225 CA; per-domain mean pLDDT 93.0 and 86.3; ASNSD1 begins MCGICCSV so Cys2 becomes Cys1 after initiator-Met excision
context: Human ASNSD1 AlphaFold DB v6 model vs E. coli AS-B crystal
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. AlphaFold models are apo and side-chain rotamers are not experimental. Refutes the seed premise that the domains or the Cys may have been lost.

citation: This run: ortholog scoring across 442 vertebrate ASNSD1 and 382 ASNS sequences (provenance/asnsd1_ortholog_conservation.csv, pos494_distribution.json)
claim_tested: Is the Glu348-equivalent carboxylate conserved in ASNSD1?
key_finding: ASNSD1 position 494: Ile 405, Met 16, Leu 4, Val 3, Thr 1, giving 0/429 acidic. ASNS position 365: Glu 376/376. Positive controls in ASNS were 100% (R49 300/300, N75 348/348, G76 87/87, E77 81/81, S363 375/375, G364 375/375)
context: UniProtKB vertebrate (taxid 7742) sequences, flank-anchored residue calling
confidence_and_limitations: High. The contrast with 376/376 Glu in ASNS and the clean positive controls makes a methodological artefact unlikely. Flank anchoring can fail on divergent sequences; unresolved species were excluded rather than guessed.

citation: This run: glutamine-pocket and P-loop conservation (provenance/asnsd1_ortholog_conservation.csv)
claim_tested: Is the loss global degeneration or specific to the synthetase step?
key_finding: Glutamine-pocket equivalents Arg57, Asn76, Glu78, Asp91 are each 99-100% conserved over 73-134 resolved species; the ATP P-loop 324-335 ILFSGGIDSMVI has S327/G328/G329/D331/S332 at 100% over 313-398 species
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. Conservation implies selection on these positions but does not demonstrate catalysis.

citation: This run: calibrated buried-cavity tunnel search (provenance/tunnel_ecoli.json, tunnel_asnsd1.json; the clearance calibration scan exceeded the executor time limit before its file was written and is reported from console output)
claim_tested: Could an intramolecular ammonia tunnel connect the two ASNSD1 sites?
key_finding: The detector recovers the AS-B tunnel at clearance <=2.4 A (28.4 A path for 22.5 A site separation). ASNSD1 is not connected at 2.4 A and gives a longer 37.2 A path at 2.0 A, where AS-B gives 27.1 A
confidence_and_limitations: Low-moderate. Apo AlphaFold models under-represent substrate-induced tunnels, which are gated. Suggestive, not decisive.

claim_tested: Does the ASNSD1 null phenotype resemble asparagine deficiency?
key_finding: Asnsd1-/- mice develop progressive degenerative myopathy with severe sarcopenia and myosteatosis; expression is maximal in skeletal muscle; no prior function had been reported for the protein
confidence_and_limitations: High for the phenotype. Absence of a brain phenotype is an argument by contrast, not a direct assay of catalysis.

claim_tested: Is the Asnsd1 phenotype metabolic and muscle-restricted?
key_finding: Asnsd1 appears among knockout lines with body fat more than 2 SD above the mean of 3651 chow-fed lines
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Screen-level data, limited per-line depth.

claim_tested: Muscle pathology in Asnsd1 loss
key_finding: Confirms muscle weakness and myosteatosis in Asnsd1 mutant mice
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate.

claim_tested: What is the ASNS loss-of-function phenotype in humans?
key_finding: Biallelic ASNS loss causes congenital microcephaly, progressive encephalopathy and intractable seizures, with other organ systems reported as unaffected
confidence_and_limitations: High for the ASNS phenotype. Used only as a contrast case.

claim_tested: Is the ASNSD1 locus the source of a separate protein?
key_finding: ASDURF, translated from a uORF in the 5'UTR of the ASNSD1 transcript, is a prefoldin-like subunit of the PAQosome
confidence_and_limitations: High. Relevant because ASDURF function is a known source of annotation carry-over onto the ASNSD1 main ORF.

claim_tested: Do family resources place ASNSD1 with asparagine synthetases?
key_finding: ASNSD1: PANTHER PTHR45937, InterPro IPR051857, N-terminal domain CDD cd03766 Gn_AT_II_novel, PF00733 hit only 513-590. ASNS/AsnB: PTHR11772, IPR050795, IPR006426 Asparagine synthase glutamine-hydrolyzing, CDD cd00712 AsnB, PF00733 235-539
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Database-level evidence, consistent with the structural result.

claim_tested: What does UniProt already assert for ASNSD1?
key_finding: Cys2 is annotated as an active site for GATase activity, but there is no CATALYTIC ACTIVITY statement and no binding-site features, unlike P08243 and P22106
confidence_and_limitations: Database-level. Consistent with a retained glutaminase motif and an unproven overall reaction.

claim_tested: Does the loss of the catalytic carboxylate predate vertebrates?
key_finding: A G-x-G-x-DE anchor validated exactly on human ASNSD1 (GIGADE, Ile494), human ASNS (GEGSDE, Glu365) and E. coli AsnB (GEGSDE, Glu349) gives 0/1731 acidic in the ASNSD1 family (InterPro IPR051857) and 1817/1869 acidic (97.2%) in the asparagine synthetase family (IPR006426). Zero acidic in Fungi 0/695, Vertebrata 0/374, Viridiplantae 0/307, Arthropoda 0/146, Nematoda 0/42, Stramenopiles 0/27, Apicomplexa 0/22, Platyhelminthes 0/18, Mollusca 0/13, Euglenozoa 0/11, Amoebozoa 0/6. Fisher exact p below double-precision resolution.
confidence_and_limitations: High. Anchor validated on three proteins with known answers. 10 percent of entries unresolved (zero or multiple motif hits) and the search was capped at 2000 entries per family, so these are large samples and not complete families.

claim_tested: Could a neighbouring carboxylate substitute for the lost residue?
key_finding: Identical acidic environments in all three structures: 1 acidic residue within 6 A of the target CB, 4 within 8 A, 4 within 10 A, with matching neighbour positions (ASNSD1 E498 5.0 A, D497 6.4 A, D537 6.5 A, D331 6.8 A; ASNS E369 5.4, D368 6.6, D401 6.8, D262 7.1; AS-B E352 5.5, D351 6.2, D384 6.2, D238 6.6). In 1CT9 the Glu348 carboxylate oxygen is 4.94 A from the AMP phosphorus.
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. Two of the three structures are predicted models and side-chain placement is not experimental.

claim_tested: Is the N-terminal Cys nucleophile universal in the ASNSD1 family?
key_finding: Met-Cys start in Vertebrata 382/423 (90.3 percent), Fungi 615/755 (81.5), Arthropoda 127/169 (75.1), Viridiplantae 271/379 (71.5), Stramenopiles 15/30, Mollusca 8/17, Platyhelminthes 9/39, Nematoda 2/56 (3.6), Apicomplexa 0/23. Inspection confirms real loss: C. elegans Q21555 begins MGIDYNRWWHLKDETLGEELKG with no Cys in the first 40 residues and no internal MC in the first 60.
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. Verified against individual N-terminal sequences rather than relying on annotation alone.

claim_tested: What GO terms are currently annotated to ASNSD1?
key_finding: Q9NWL6 has 28 annotation lines over 4 terms: GO:0003674, GO:0005575 and GO:0008150 all ND (BHF-UCL, GO_REF:0000015) plus GO:0005515 protein binding (IPI, IntAct). GO:0004066, GO:0006529, GO:0070981, GO:0016884 and GO:0005524 are absent. P08243 has 24 lines over 9 terms including GO:0004066 with IDA, IBA and IEA; the IBA propagates through PANTHER subfamily PTN000206334 in PTHR11772, which does not contain ASNSD1.
context: EBI QuickGO, retrieved during this run
confidence_and_limitations: High for the state at retrieval. GO content changes over time, so the curator should re-check before acting.

evidence_type: primary, in vitro holdup and peptide array plus cell-based AP-MS
stance: competing explanation for the only informative annotation
claim_tested: What does ASNSD1 bind, and does it justify a more specific term than protein binding?
key_finding: All 22 recorded partners contain PDZ domains (98 PDZ domains in total): GRID2IP, MPDZ, DLG4, APBA1, TJP1, DLG1, SNTB1, IL16, SCRIB, PDZK1, FRMPD2, MAGI2, NHERF4, LNX2, PATJ, LNX1, DLG3, MAGI1, APBA2, GRIP2, WHRN, GRIP1. Human ASNSD1 ends LENLSIEKETKL, a class I PDZ-binding motif; human ASNS ends RTLTHYKSAVKA and has none. 22 partners come from the holdup assay, 2 of those also from the peptide array, and PDZK1 independently from BioPlex AP-MS.
context: Human proteins; mostly isolated C-terminal peptides in vitro
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. One in vitro assay dominates and peptide-based affinity measures motif capacity rather than an in-cell complex. PDZK1 is the only cell-based corroboration.

claim_tested: Is the class I PDZ-binding motif conserved across vertebrates?
key_finding: Only 12/437 full-length-like vertebrate ASNSD1 orthologs end in a class I motif and only 10 end in ETKL. Human, chimpanzee and both macaques end ETKL or DTKL; mouse and rat end GRLQILP, cow LSVEN, chicken SRLKLF, zebrafish RLVTTI, Xenopus MAGSKE. Commonest C-termini are KLLS (116) and KLFS (91), with Ser at position 0 in 236/437.
context: UniProtKB vertebrate orthologs, entries of 550-750 residues
confidence_and_limitations: High. Length filter excludes fragments. Shows the motif is primate-restricted and must not be propagated by orthology.
